inputs.name: Day's filter sentence
inputs.value: none below 0.65; full stack 0.64 on 10 genes

day.reading: 0.80 is a property of the full gene set and the 0.23 an artefact of a curated subset
day.holds: his gene-set arithmetic is right (6,946 = 34.05%, 1.516); the gene-set effect has his sign on both assemblies (+31% on hg38, +14% on T2T); CSAC did select on alignment quality and coverage

critic.reading: a correct extraction gives about 0.27 on all genes and 0.21-0.24 on one2one genes
critic.holds: 0.80 is 2.95x the measured all-gene value; no correct-frame computation reaches it (0.15-0.45); all 32 filter stacks sit at 0.214-0.283; Day's own two single-SNV figures imply N/S 3.55 against a measured 3.34, and his full stack (0.64) is already below his 0.65 floor

notes: Data-check object; no verdict moves. What Day's pipeline did to reach 0.80 cannot be settled without his code, gene list or per-gene table (unreleased; DN1 internal stays pending), but that is DN1's internal verdict, not this object's measurement: the genome-wide value and its sensitivity to gene set and filters are measured twice (L1, L1b). Day's '6,946 thrown out' sets his 20,400 against CSAC's 13,454; CSAC's own start was 16,045 genes, of which its curation removed 2,591 (16.2%). L1's 0.207 is the one2one value on hg38/panTro5; the T2T value is 0.238 (L1b).
